title: Oath and Garden Anew
premise: Lior Zhou has spent a decade burying their beast-speaker gift beneath harmless charms in Vellamark, a city where magic is outlawed and informants are paid in bread. When a feral child named Sef arrives speaking the First Tongue—the language that once commanded beasts to war—Lior realizes the child is a living vessel of the old pact, and that the crown's Wardens have begun hunting anyone the beasts remember. Fleeing into the wild garden-ruins beyond the walls, Lior must choose between destroying Sef's gift to keep them both safe, or rekindling the ancient covenant and paying the blood-price it demands. In the end, Lior speaks the First Tongue aloud, offering their own memories as the price of survival, and the beasts accept: Sef lives free, the war stays buried, and Lior returns to the city with a decade of their past gone—remembering the child, but not why they ever swore to hide.
about_author: Ulyana Iversen is the pen name of a former botanist who spent six years cataloguing endangered meadowlands before turning to fiction. Her work blends folkloric fantasy with quiet, aching questions about what we owe the past.

chapters.title: The Charm-Seller's Door
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A cold morning of selling luck-knots in Vellamark's gray market establishes Lior's careful, hidden life—until a barefoot child collapses at their door, speaking words the market beasts answer to. The emotional beat is dread disguised as routine; Lior's decade of silence cracks open in a single evening.

chapters.title: A Language Older Than Walls
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior hides Sef in their cellar and confirms the impossible: the child speaks the First Tongue, and the rats and pigeons obey it. A Warden's knock at the door forces Lior to use a charm to deceive a man for the first time in ten years. The beat is terror mixed with an unwelcome thrill of remembered power.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Burn
chapters.summary: Sef's POV, fragmented and sensory. Through the child's eyes we see the raid on the village that raised them, the Warden-captain Ashk taking the village's speaker alive, and Sef's flight. The beat is grief rendered without adult vocabulary—fire, teeth, and a promise Sef made to a dying woman.

chapters.title: The Garden Beneath the City
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior seeks out Maren, an old fence who once trafficked in forbidden things, and learns the Wardens are following beast-sign through the city—someone's gift is betraying them. Maren gives Lior a map to the garden-ruins and a warning: the beasts remember everyone who ever spoke. The beat is the past tightening its grip.

chapters.title: Flight Through Root and Stone
chapters.summary: Alternating Lior and Sef POV. The escape through Vellamark's underways goes wrong when Sef instinctively calls a tunnel-beast to help, revealing them both. Lior's fury and fear collide with Sef's bewildered sense that the beasts are friends. The beat is trust fraying—Lior realizes the child's gift cannot simply be suppressed.

chapters.title: The Ruined Conservatory
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, with Sef's interludes. In the overgrown garden-ruins they find the last of the old speakers' order, a half-mad gardener named Ovid who tends graves instead of plants. Ovid explains the covenant: the beasts ended the war in exchange for the speakers' memories, and a vessel of the First Tongue means the debt can be called again. The beat is the weight of inheritance made explicit.

chapters.title: Ashk at the Gate
chapters.summary: Ashk's POV. The Warden-captain, herself a failed speaker whose gift was burned out of her, closes on the ruins with a company of soldiers and a captured beast used as a bloodhound. Her chapters reveal the crown's true fear—not magic, but the beasts' collective memory of the throne's founding crime. The beat is a villain with a wound where her gift used to be.

chapters.title: The Calling of Debts
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The Wardens breach the conservatory; Ovid dies holding the gate of thorns, and Sef, terrified, involuntarily calls every beast in the region—the ancient war nearly reignites in a single night of screaming wings. Lior must calm the gathering horde with the only currency left: their own memories. The beat is sacrifice chosen in the middle of catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Price Spoken Aloud
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, dissolving into the First Tongue. Lior offers ten years of memory to the beasts as payment for Sef's freedom; the horde accepts, and Ashk, witnessing her old gift stir at the sound of the Tongue, lowers her blade and lets them go—then turns her company back to the city, carrying the throne's crime in her silence. The beat is awe and terrible cost intertwined.

chapters.title: Oath and Garden Anew
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, quieter now. Lior returns to Vellamark with a decade missing, selling charms again, watched over from the rooftops by beasts that know them though they cannot say why. Sef, free in the wild gardens, visits each season. The final image: Lior plants a seed from Ovid's conservatory and feels, without understanding, that they kept a promise. The beat is bittersweet peace—survival paid for, and worth it.
